## Election order and the AI shadow war (July 2026)

A federal appeals court in late July 2026 blocked key portions of Trump's executive order on election administration in 23 Democrat-led states, ruling the administration could not enforce several provisions while litigation continued; the order had sought proof-of-citizenship measures and restrictions affecting mail voting, and the decision set up a likely Supreme Court fight over presidential authority to regulate federal elections.[{n}] Badlands commentary framed the dispute as one of presidential authorities, a category of battle that has largely gone Trump's way, and asked who is constitutionally authorized to exercise the Postal Service's decision rights if neither the states nor the President may.[{n}]

On artificial intelligence, [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] argued that Trump has "very clearly" pinned a good degree of his futurism goals on the perpetuation and acceleration of AI, and that Chinese releases of open-weight models grant Trump the narrative shielding needed to resist the regulation push from [[openai|OpenAI]] and [[anthropic|Anthropic]].[{n}] Trump's Commerce Secretary [[howard-lutnick|Howard Lutnick]] reportedly said the administration aims to "protect open source AI."[{n}]

In foreign policy, Trump praised [[turkey|Turkey]] as a "tremendous ally" while publicly criticizing Israeli military operations during a meeting with [[benjamin-netanyahu|Benjamin Netanyahu]], and his administration intensified its campaign against Mexican drug cartels, indicting ten Mexican government officials over alleged links to the [[sinaloa-cartel|Sinaloa cartel]].[{n}]

## Trump election order (2026)

The appeals court decision of July 2026 preserving the injunction against President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]]'s election administration executive order in 23 Democrat-led states was reported as setting up a likely Supreme Court showdown over the scope of presidential authority in regulating federal elections and the balance of power between the federal government and the states.[{n}] Badlands commentary noted that the Court would be deciding "dangerously close to the midterms," observed that history suggests the justices decline to make changes so near an election, and allowed that they have surprised observers before.[{n}]

## 2026 executive order litigation

President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]]'s executive order on election administration sought to impose new federal requirements affecting mail voting, including instructing the [[united-states-postal-service|US Postal Service]] to establish new standards for mail-in ballots, alongside proof-of-citizenship measures.[{n}] A federal appeals court blocked key portions of the order in 23 Democrat-led states in July 2026, leaving the district court injunction intact pending litigation and setting up a probable Supreme Court fight.[{n}]
